markdown_report:
### Insights

**Starting point.** (1) The diagnosis suggests weak aggregation of repeated recent interests, but training margins cannot establish their influence. Controlled interventions measure model dependence, not verified user needs. (2) Broad relevance can conceal unsupported compatibility assumptions. Titles/descriptions permit limited evidence checks; missing specifications require abstention. (3) Architecture-independent scoring hooks support comparable diagnostics, provided masking semantics are verified for each encoder.

**Related work.** (1) CETRec separates recency from relative order [1]; evidence removal and order rearrangement therefore require separate experiments. (2) Sampling-reliability research distinguishes sampled and full-catalog evaluation [2]; pinned macro validation HR@10 remains the selection criterion. (3) TREC separates compatibility from complementarity [3], motivating explicit unknown labels. (4) CauseRec motivates interest-level interventions, while RLS motivates generic-corruption controls [4,5]; neither validates this proposed protocol. (5) Lexical similarity can reflect boilerplate, and cluster stability alone does not establish meaningful interests [8,9].

### Directions and framework

| Direction | Existing signal | Proposed addition | Interpretation boundary |
|---|---|---|---|
| Interest aggregation | Training margins | Matched history masking | Model dependence on operationalized groups |
| Temporal reasoning | Sequence scores | Separate order-only perturbations | Positional sensitivity |
| Product usefulness | Text similarity | Evidence spans and abstention | Documented compatibility only |
| Diagnostic validity | Embedding similarity | Mask invariance and lexical nulls | Implementation correctness and proxy validity |

### Candidate ideas

Scores are originality/potential/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Each assessment includes a benefit (+) and limitation (−).

| Idea | Originality | Potential | Difficulty |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Matched evidence masking** [1,4,5] | 5: + controlled combination; − familiar interventions | 7: + guides ablations; − unvalidated link to HR@10 | 5: + existing hooks; − masking and matching need care |
| Recency-weighted history residual added to SASRec | 4: + targeted aggregation; − standard pooling | 7: + inexpensive accuracy ablation; − may amplify redundant interests | 4: + small module; − predictor changes |
| Text-supported compatibility audit [3] | 5: + explicit abstention; − established taxonomy | 6: + interpretable errors; − sparse specifications | 6: + simple rules possible; − annotation burden |

### Selected idea: matched evidence masking

At 0% progress, retain the diagnostic as the first step; use the recency residual as a subsequent model ablation. The diagnostic itself promises no accuracy gain.

Fit per-category TF–IDF on training-interaction items’ available titles/descriptions: lowercase, word unigrams/bigrams, `min_df=2`, `max_df=0.95`, sublinear term frequency, L2 normalization. Within each model-truncated history, greedily group recent events whose pairwise cosine similarity is at least 0.3, breaking ties by original position. Require two distinct item IDs within the latest 20 events; select the largest group, then the most recent. Treat these as lexical evidence groups, not established intentions.

For each group, sample 20 same-user control masks without replacement within each mask. Match cardinality and joint counts across normalized-position quartiles, training-popularity quartiles, and within-history item-frequency bins of 1 versus ≥2. Exclude the identical target mask; retain overlaps and report them. Skip unmatched users without relaxing criteria, reporting coverage and balance. Matching may restrict conclusions to a small eligible subset.

```text
freeze weights; cache original scores
for each eligible user:
    construct targeted mask and matched controls
    rescore with identical position-preserving semantics
    subtract mean control effect from targeted effect
bootstrap users within category; average categories equally
```

Use separate padding/intervention masks, erase removed item identity before the first block, exclude removed keys at every layer, and retain original positions and readout index. A removed readout retains only its positional neutral query. Fully masked attention rows require an explicit finite-output branch [6,7]. Verify removed-ID invariance with dropout disabled; zero padding alone is insufficient.

Keep targets, candidates, seen-item exclusions, and item-ID tie-breaking fixed. Report Δrank, top-10 exit conditional on original inclusion, and overlap/10; optionally Jaccard and rank-biased overlap. Compare isolated-event masks, prefix shuffles retaining the latest item, and deletion/repacking separately. With seed 42, bootstrap users 1,000 times, grouping their interventions; intervals condition on fixed weights and candidates.

Check missing text, top terms, near-duplicates, title-only/description-only agreement, boilerplate removal, and within-category item-to-text permutation nulls; order shuffling tests temporal persistence separately. These checks address lexical shortcuts, not ownership or causal preferences. Keep twenty-user full-catalog feedback exploratory; select model changes exclusively through pinned macro validation HR@10 and record diagnostic GPU cost.

References: [1] [CETRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.03047); [2] [Sampling reliability](https://doi.org/10.1145/3705328.3748086); [3] [TREC recommendations](https://trec-product-search.github.io/recommendations.html); [4] [CauseRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.05261); [5] [RLS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.12686); [6] [PyTorch attention](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.modules.activation.MultiheadAttention.html); [7] [Attention tutorial](https://docs.pytorch.org/tutorials/intermediate/transformer_building_blocks.html); [8] [Text clustering](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/auto_examples/text/plot_document_clustering.html); [9] [Consensus-clustering limitations](https://www.nature.com/articles/srep06207).

idea.description: Implement matched evidence masking in the compatibility-preserving DiagnosisProbe to estimate recommendation dependence on repeated recent lexical evidence beyond matched generic history corruption.
idea.motivation: Qualitative feedback suggests broad associations and isolated purchases dominate recommendations, while existing embedding and margin probes cannot identify influential history evidence. At initial research progress, a bounded diagnostic can guide subsequent model ablations, but it does not itself improve HR@10 or establish actual user intentions. Recency-weighted history pooling remains a practical follow-up candidate.
idea.implementation_notes: Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions. Use view.model as the actual trained module; save and restore its training state and run inference without gradients. Preserve view.item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data, and review_data. Add an optional architecture-specific intervention hook without breaking existing calls. Remove intervened item identity before the first encoder block, retain original positional indices, mask removed slots as attention keys in every layer, and preserve the baseline readout index. Define a removed readout as a neutral positional query. Explicitly handle attention rows with no allowed keys; multiplication by zero does not repair NaNs. Verify finite outputs for empty histories, equality of baseline and no-intervention outputs, and invariance to substituted IDs at removed positions with dropout disabled. Unsupported architectures must return unavailable diagnostics rather than silently use deletion. Construct text features, popularity counts, and matching bins from training data only; ignore unavailable ratings, reviews, categories, prices, stores, and simulator traits. Preserve existing collapse and margin metrics, explaining that mapped cosine similarity near 0.5 is not proof of collapse; return unavailable statistics with observation counts for empty samples. Replace unavailable category-error breakdowns with explicit unavailability rather than fabricated labels. Preserve all four routes, DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, the SASREC_EPOCHS environment override with default 200, single-GPU execution, and trial-local artifacts. Diagnostic GPU time counts against the shared budget. This diagnostic requires no production predictor change; any subsequent architecture change must update the predictor writer and working/predict.py consistently.
idea.pseudocode: Predeclare diagnostic settings before inspecting outcomes: seed 42; up to 50 uniformly sampled training users per category without replacement; model-truncated histories; latest 20 events for group discovery; cosine threshold 0.3; 20 controls per eligible user; 1,000 user-bootstrap replicates. Fit category-specific training-item TF-IDF with lowercase word unigrams/bigrams, min_df=2, max_df=0.95, sublinear TF, and L2 normalization; flag empty vocabularies as unavailable. Process recent nonempty-text events from latest to earliest, assigning each to the first group for which cosine similarity to every member is >=0.3, or start a group; require at least two distinct item IDs. Choose the largest eligible group, breaking ties by latest member and then original positions. Compute normalized-position quartiles using slot index divided by maximum sequence length; compute popularity quartiles from training-item counts with a documented deterministic quantile method and repeated-item frequency from the truncated history. Generate 20 distinct same-user control sets with the same joint-bin counts and cardinality as the target mask; exclude the identical target set, allow and report partial overlap, and mark users unavailable if insufficient distinct controls exist. Freeze the original full-catalog unseen-item candidate set for sampled training users; exclude the original observed history in every condition and break score ties by ascending item ID. Do not manufacture next-item targets for training-only histories: report top-10 overlap there. If a separate legal validation diagnostic interface is supplied, keep its original target and pinned candidates fixed and report rank_masked-rank_original and top-10 exits conditional on original inclusion; otherwise mark target metrics unavailable. Rescore target and control masks using identical validated masking semantics. Report raw effects and each user's target effect minus mean control effect; for overlap use 1-overlap as the effect direction. Bootstrap users within each category, preserving all their interventions, then equally average category means; do not silently drop an unavailable category from a claimed four-category macro statistic. Separately evaluate singleton lexical groups with singleton matched controls, prefix shuffling preserving the latest item, and deletion/repacking. Fix and log their seeds and permutations. Run prespecified lexical sensitivity checks with title-only and description-only features, removal of phrases occurring in at least half of available training-item documents, top-term and near-duplicate inspection, and 20 item-to-text permutations within each category. Report these as exploratory proxy-validity checks, with coverage and runtime; do not select thresholds by strongest diagnostic effect. Use only the unchanged host macro validation HR@10 to select subsequent trained models.

originality.positive: Combines interest-specific history interventions, matched corruption controls, lexical nulls, and architecture-compatible masking in one focused diagnostic.
originality.negative: History perturbation, interest grouping, and matched controls are established methods; the contribution is a careful adaptation rather than a new causal identification method.

future_potential.positive: Can distinguish dependence on repeated lexical evidence from sensitivity to generic corruption and motivate targeted pooling or training-objective ablations.
future_potential.negative: Lexical groups may encode brands or boilerplate, strict matching may limit coverage, and diagnostic improvements need not predict higher validation HR@10.

code_difficulty.positive: Reuses existing scoring hooks and sparse text features without external data, pretrained encoders, or an additional trained model.
code_difficulty.negative: Correct residual-stream masking, safe empty attention rows, reproducible control sampling, fixed exclusions, and user-level uncertainty require meaningful implementation and verification.

related_work.title: CETRec (2025)
contributions: The supplied research summary describes separate treatment of recency and relative interaction order through counterfactual tuning.
limitations: Its LLM recommender setting does not establish effectiveness for SASRec on the four matched Amazon datasets.
It does not validate the proposed matched masking protocol.

related_work.title: On the Reliability of Sampling Strategies (2025)
contributions: Distinguishes properties of sampled evaluation, including agreement with full-catalog ranking and robustness to exposure bias.
limitations: Does not make supplementary full-catalog diagnostics interchangeable with the pinned sampled benchmark.
Diagnostic bootstrap intervals exclude training and candidate-sampling uncertainty.

related_work.title: TREC 2025 Product Recommendation Guidelines
contributions: Provides a vocabulary separating substitutes, complements, unrelated items, and unassessable relationships, including compatibility distinctions.
limitations: Relationship judgments require supporting information and cannot establish current ownership or replacement intent.
Sparse titles and descriptions may require frequent abstention.

related_work.title: CauseRec
contributions: Distinguishes indispensable and dispensable item or interest concepts and uses counterfactual replacements in representation learning.
limitations: Motivates interest-level interventions but does not validate this fixed-model matched-control diagnostic or identify actual user preferences.

related_work.title: Rank List Sensitivity research
contributions: Studies recommendation instability under interaction perturbations, motivating measurement of generic corruption effects and ranking changes.
limitations: Training-data perturbations differ from inference-time masking with frozen model weights.

related_work.title: PyTorch MultiheadAttention documentation
contributions: Documents attention masks and the convention that True in key_padding_mask excludes a key.
limitations: Key masking alone does not remove item identity from queries or residual streams.
Position-preserving interventions require architecture-specific implementation beyond the documented interface.

related_work.title: PyTorch transformer building blocks tutorial
contributions: Provides implementation context for attention behavior and numerical handling.
limitations: Fully masked attention behavior must be verified for the installed version and actual execution path.

related_work.title: Scikit-learn text document clustering example
contributions: Provides practical sparse text representation and clustering methods and illustrates removal of distracting document metadata.
limitations: Lexical similarity does not establish sustained user preference or product compatibility.
Amazon brand, model, and boilerplate shortcuts remain hypotheses requiring task-specific checks.

related_work.title: Consensus-clustering limitations study
contributions: Shows that apparent cluster stability can arise without genuine underlying groups.
limitations: Does not establish that the proposed Amazon lexical groups are spurious; it motivates null controls rather than a predetermined conclusion.
